subject: MAP: POC activation blueprint — org, API keys, allowlist & peering
messages:
From: Mateo Alvarez <mateo_alvarez@redwood.com>
To: Dana Ross <dana.ross@vitascale.com>, VitaScale PoC Team <poc@vitascale.com>
Cc: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 4 Aug 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: MAP: POC activation blueprint — org, API keys, allowlist & peering

Hi Dana / VitaScale team,

Thanks for agreeing to run the 3-week pilot with Redwood. Attached is a short MAP workbook that breaks the POC into discrete workstreams. To keep the activation on a tight timeline (close target: 2026-08-20), we need to lock the items below this week. Can you confirm owners and ETA per-row in the attached MAP?

Key asks to unblock provisioning:
1) Org onboarding: Can VitaScale confirm the canonical org name and primary admin email so we can create a customer org in our control plane? We need: org_name, admin_email, preferred region (us-east/us-west).
2) API keys & service account: We recommend a dedicated service account for the POC with an API key scoped to generation/chat endpoints. We support both long-lived API keys and short-lived (ephemeral) keys via our SDK. Please let us know which you prefer. If long-lived, we’ll provide instructions for rotation cadence.
3) IP allowlisting: For firewall rules, please allow Redwood outbound and inbound endpoints. For the POC we typically ask customers to allow these two CIDR blocks: 52.23.14.0/24 and 35.196.200.0/24 (send/receive to our hosted runtime). If you require a more formal IP list (multiple regions), we can share a larger table — confirm.
4) VPC peering (optional but recommended for private traffic): If you want private peering, please share the VPC CIDR and the cloud account ID we should peer to (we will initiate from our side). Typical questions we need: VPC CIDR, route table that will accept peering, any mandatory security groups or NACLs to pre-open.

Proposed milestones (high level)
- 2026-08-04: MAP workbook + kickoff (this thread)
- 2026-08-07: Org created + API key(s) delivered to PoC service account
- 2026-08-10: Network allowlist verified (connectivity smoke test)
- 2026-08-12: First inference run (canary requests)
- 2026-08-20: POC acceptance / close (technical sign-off)

Attachments: MAP_Workstream_v1.xlsx (workstream + owners), vpc-network-diagram.pdf (example).

Notes / open items: if you have a security contact, please loop them in (we will send a short Soc2 summary and our network peering checklist). Also flag any procurement/PO details early if you expect billing approvals before the 8/20 close.

Happy to sync live — propose a 30-min tech kick on Fri 2026-08-06 or Mon 2026-08-09.

Regards,
Mateo Alvarez
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
mateo_alvarez@redwood.com

From: Dana Ross <dana.ross@vitascale.com>
To: Mateo Alvarez <mateo_alvarez@redwood.com>
Cc: VitaScale PoC Team <poc@vitascale.com>
Date: Tue, 4 Aug 2026 11:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: MAP: POC activation blueprint — org, API keys, allowlist & peering

Thanks Mateo — this looks good and granular, appreciate the roadmap. Quick answers and questions from our side: 

- Org info: org_name = "VitaScale Labs - Redwood POC", admin_email = "dana.ross@vitascale.com", region = "us-west-2".
- VPC CIDR: 10.60.0.0/16 (AWS account 987654321012). We can open peering if you provide the accepter account ID and proposed CIDR for your side.
- IP allowlist: we can add two /24s but need a formal list to submit to security. Can you confirm the authoritative source of IPs (do they change during the POC)?
- API keys: security prefers ephemeral tokens when possible, but for integration tests we need at least one long-lived key. Can you provide guidance on the recommended rotation TTL?

Security contact: Priya Mehta (secops@vitascale.com). She’ll want the SOC2 summary and a network peering checklist before we proceed with peering.

We can do the tech kickoff on Fri 2026-08-06 at 10:00 PT — works for our engineers. If that time is OK, please send a calendar invite.

—Dana
Dana Ross
Head of Infrastructure | VitaScale Labs
dana.ross@vitascale.com

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Dana Ross <dana.ross@vitascale.com>, Mateo Alvarez <mateo_alvarez@redwood.com>
Cc: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 5 Aug 2026 08:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: MAP: POC activation blueprint — org, API keys, allowlist & peering

On Tue, Aug 4, 2026 at 11:05 AM Dana Ross <dana.ross@vitascale.com> wrote:
> - IP allowlist: we can add two /24s but need a formal list to submit to security. Can you confirm the authoritative source of IPs (do they change during the POC)?

Hi Dana — quick technical follow-up with concrete items you can give to your security team.

1) IPs for the hosted POC (authoritative for us during the pilot): 52.23.14.0/24 and 35.196.200.0/24. These are our runtime egress/ingress for the US region we're proposing. We will notify you if we need to add region-specific blocks, but for the 2-week pilot these two cover the hosted path.

2) API keys: recommended pattern for pilots — create:
   • One long-lived service API key (scoped) for CI/integration (rotate every 90 days).
   • Ephemeral tokens for client-side workloads or user sessions (TTL 15 minutes — minted via SDK).
We can provide a small script to rotate and map keys into your secrets manager if preferred.

3) VPC peering checklist (summary):
   • We will initiate the peering request from Redwood account ID 123456789012.
   • Provide your VPC ID and the route table you want updated (we will add a route for 10.60.0.0/16 pointing to the peering connection).
   • Security groups: open TCP 443 between your app subnet and our peered subnet for private API calls.
   • No overlapping CIDRs required (your 10.60.0.0/16 is fine).

4) Canary approach: for the first 24 hours of the POC we recommend routing 5% of traffic to a smaller model variant (rwd-small-q4) to validate accuracy and tail latency before hitting the full model. This reduces token cost risk while you validate outputs.

Attaching the vpc-network-diagram.pdf (referenced in Mateo's MAP) and a short runbook we use for peering acceptance in the attachments section of the kickoff invite.

If Friday at 10:00 PT works, we’ll send the invite with a short tech agenda (1) credentials + org handoff, (2) connectivity tests, (3) first inference canary.

Thanks,
Karthik Iyer
Infra Lead, Redwood Inference
karthik_iyer@redwood.com

From: Dana Ross <dana.ross@vitascale.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Mateo Alvarez <mateo_alvarez@redwood.com>
Cc: Priya Mehta <secops@vitascale.com>, VitaScale PoC Team <poc@vitascale.com>
Date: Thu, 6 Aug 2026 15:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: MAP: POC activation blueprint — org, API keys, allowlist & peering

Perfect — thank you both.

- We’ll open the two /24s in our perimeter firewall this afternoon (52.23.14.0/24, 35.196.200.0/24) and Priya will validate.
- We’ll create the long-lived service key for CI (rotation every 90 days) and are interested in the ephemeral flow for session workloads — please send the SDK snippet.
- Peering: I confirmed internal approval for peering; I’ll send the VPC ID + route table by tomorrow morning.

Friday 2026-08-06, 10:00 PT is good — calendar invite accepted. Our expectation is the POC will close on or before 2026-08-20 pending the canary results and a short acceptance doc.

Priya (cc): I’ve added you for the SOC2/network checklist items — will you coordinate with Mateo on what you need?

Thanks,
Dana
